cross_task_notes.InputBuffer::push_char: TASK-1.02.02 chose 'append at end + caret follows to end'. Phase 1 defers character-level caret editing, so insertion never happens at the caret. If TASK-1.03.07 wants insertion-at-caret, that is an interface decision (~5 lines).
cross_task_notes.BackspaceOutcome::BufferEmpty: Means 'the buffer is empty after this key', NOT 'a syllable was removed'. The nihaoa -> nihao -> ni -> "" sequence yields RemovedSyllable, RemovedSyllable, BufferEmpty. TASK-1.03.07 must not expect RemovedSyllable on the clearing press.
cross_task_notes.backspace at caret 0: Deletes the character the caret points at. The card left this boundary undefined; returning BufferEmpty would end the session on non-empty input and lose the preedit.
cross_task_notes.InputBuffer::set_boundaries: Call it only when segmentation succeeded (best_segmentation_hint returned true). Passing the pass-through whole-string grid [0, len] on failure makes one Backspace delete the entire input. TASK-1.03.07 and TASK-1.02.05 must respect this.
cross_task_notes.InputBuffer timestamps: ime-core may not read the clock (0.4 rule 4), so the struct exposes mark_session_start(at_unix_ms) / started_at_unix_ms(); the caller stamps it. Field stays 0 until stamped.
cross_task_notes.criterion case-name collision: The input-buffer bench and the decode bench both want a case named input/buffer_ops. If TASK-1.02.07 also emits it, keep one to avoid duplicate criterion directories.
cross_task_notes.PassthroughFlags gained a fifth field: TASK-1.02.06 added `temp_english: bool` (default false) to PassthroughFlags. It is session state, not a config key, but the card's rule 4 is a state guard and is unreachable inside the pure classifier without it. The four config-backed fields match the card's defaults exactly, so TASK-1.03.06 can still build the struct with ..Default::default().
cross_task_notes.passthrough rule order: The temp-English guard is evaluated BEFORE the uppercase-commit and URL rules, not fourth as the card lists. In the card's literal order, one uppercase letter in temp-English mode would hit rule 3, commit that letter and exit the session -- exactly what the mode exists to prevent.
cross_task_notes.EnterTempEnglish is not returned by clas: A pure text classifier cannot observe a key chord, so the router (TASK-1.04.04) produces EnterTempEnglish and the session machine owns the flag. classify returns the other three variants; is_consumed() reports EnterTempEnglish as consumed.
cross_task_notes.English punctuation mode returns HostHan: For the twelve ASCII marks under punct_mode = english, classify returns HostHandles rather than the card's fallback Decode. Decode would hand the mark to the normaliser, which discards it as an illegal input character, so pressing a comma would do nothing at all. Host passthrough types it as-is.
cross_task_notes.double quote pairing: The card maps the double quote to two targets. With no keystroke memory, classify pairs it using the unclosed-quote count in the surrounding text and degrades to the opening quote when the host reports none.
cross_task_notes.benchmark methodology: Do NOT trust criterion numbers taken while sub-agents are running. passthrough/classify measured 511ns under load and 726ns on a re-run minutes later, and criterion itself reported a bogus +40% regression. Every budget measurement must be re-taken on an idle machine.
cross_task_notes.check-unsafe SAFETY proximity: check-unsafe.sh looks back SAFETY_LOOKBACK = 5 lines from an `unsafe` block. crates/ime-dict/src/mmap.rs's static_bytes has its `// SAFETY:` line 6 lines above the block, so the audit reports it as undocumented. Fix by tightening that comment block by one line so the marker lands inside the window (the file's other unsafe block passes because its marker is exactly at the boundary). Deferred until the TASK-1.03.03 agent, which owns mmap.rs right now, stops editing it.
cross_task_notes.preedit segmentation line source: TASK-1.02.05's build_preedit(buf, dag) can only see the SyllableDag, so the syllable separators come from best_segmentation_hint (fewest syllables, ties to the longer syllable), NOT from the Viterbi winner's decoded.segments -- which the caller does have at state/machine.rs:445 and does not pass in. Decision (main agent): keep the hint. The preedit is a view of the INPUT, not of the top candidate: the maximal-munch reading is stable across keystrokes, while a separator driven by the winning path would re-draw every time the ranking changed, which is visible flicker under the user's eyes. Concretely `xian` stays one syllable even when the top candidate is 西安 (xi|an). If a later card wants the preedit to preview the winning segmentation, that is a signature change to build_preedit and an interface decision, not a bug fix.
cross_task_notes.Preedit.dropped is deliberately absent: TASK-1.02.05's rule 4 asks for dropped characters to be recorded on Preedit.dropped. Preedit is a frozen ime-types type and has no such field. Decision (main agent): do NOT add one. The information is not lost -- SyllableDag::dropped_chars() carries it with raw offsets and first_error() turns it into decode/invalid-char -- and Preedit is the payload the UI thread draws every frame, so a diagnostics-only field there would be dead weight on the hot path. Adding it would be a frozen-contract change needing its own ADR.
cross_task_notes.TASK-1.02.04 NFR conflicts with its own: The card's NFR asks for <=3 temporary allocations per decode with buffer reuse, but it also freezes decode(&self, ...) and documents Decoder as Send + Sync and reentrant; a buffer owned by the decoder needs &mut self or interior mutability. Measured reality: Decoder holds {cfg, scorer} and no buffer, so a decode makes 5-8 temporary allocations. This is not a defect of TASK-1.02.04 -- it is exactly what PERF-P0.01.01 (DecodeScratch, anchored on viterbi/decoder.rs) exists to fix, by threading an explicit scratch object through the call. Recorded so the perf card inherits the requirement.
cross_task_notes.preedit 3a is arithmetically wrong in th: TASK-1.02.05's DoD 3a claims text.len() <= 96 for a 64-byte raw input, on the reasoning that at most 32 separators are inserted. Wrong: 64 one-byte syllables need 63 separators, so the real bound is 127 = 2*64-1 (reached exactly by `lvlvlv`). The code does not truncate -- truncating would hide what the user typed -- and the module doc now records the true bound. The header is expected to clip from the left instead.
cross_task_notes.TASK-1.02.05 spans ordering: The card's invariant 'spans strictly ascending by start' is unsatisfiable as written: its own implementation step 2 wants a zero-width cursor span at start == end == caret, and the caret may sit at 0 or at a syllable start, so a zero-width span and a span beginning at that same offset necessarily share a start. The implemented and documented reading is 'ordered, with a zero-width Cursor span allowed to tie with a span at the same offset'; the randomised test asserts exactly that.
cross_task_notes.lm_holdout.tsv attribution: features.md 6.1.1 and R-08 record tests/fixtures/lm_holdout.tsv (>=5000 rows) against TASK-1.02.04, but that card's body and DoD never mention it. The file exists and its generator is xtask/src/tune/holdout.rs, i.e. it belongs to the tuning chain of TASK-1.02.03. Recorded so the acceptance record does not credit the wrong card.

cross_task_notes.UiSurface no longer requires Send: UI-OPT-P0.02.02 found that `pub trait UiSurface: Send` (crates/ime-ui/src/ui_thread/surface.rs) cannot be implemented by any surface that owns the Slint platform, because RspinyinPlatform holds an Rc and the component handle is reference counted. The old doc justified the bound as 'free to own a display connection that another thread could have created', but that is not what Send buys: the Box<dyn UiSurface> is built by the factory, which the UI thread runs, and consumed by the UI loop on the same thread, so it never crosses a boundary. DECISION (main agent): drop the bound. What it cost was the production surface; what it protected against is enforced where it belongs, by requiring a connection to be created on the thread that will poll it. CandidateSurface now impls UiSurface.
cross_task_notes.candidate.slint must re-export Theme: slint_build::compile generates Rust only for the roots reachable from the file it is handed: the Window component and the globals DECLARED IN THAT FILE. A global the file merely imports stays private to the import graph and gets no Rust accessor -- so include_modules! produced a module with CandidateWindow and CandidateMetrics and no Theme at all, and crates/ime-ui/src/adapter.rs could not write the palette into the component. Fixed by adding `export { Theme } from "theme.slint";` to ui/candidate.slint. Verified: the generated file now carries `pub struct Theme`. Any future .slint global that Rust has to reach needs the same re-export.
cross_task_notes.TASK-1.05.04 found 7 alpha bytes that di: ui/theme.slint and src/theme.rs both claimed to be byte-identical and were not: 7 tokens differed by 1/255. Cause is that Slint converts alpha two different ways -- i-slint-compiler's rgba() builtin truncates (`(255. * a).max(0.).min(255.) as u8`) while i-slint-core's with_alpha() rounds (`(alpha * 255.).round() as u8`). The Rust side was moved to the value the renderer actually draws, per token, with a comment. If the project ever decides rounding is authoritative instead, both the bytes and the new consistency test's evaluation rule have to change together -- they cannot disagree.
cross_task_notes.PERF-P0.02.01 deviates from its card on: The card says hydrated may only go true -> false in degrade(). The agent deliberately did not flip it there, and the reasoning holds: counts holds only values that reached the file, a failed transaction rolled back, so counts still equals the file and flipping the flag would make a read-only store start opening read transactions on the decode hot path -- the exact opposite of the card's purpose. Documented in degrade()'s doc comment. hydrated is therefore a plain bool fixed at open, so the hot path needs no lock for it.
cross_task_notes.PERF-P0.02.01 HYDRATE_CAP vs the 2MB RSS: The card's DoD 3 asks for <= 2MB of RSS growth after hydrating HYDRATE_CAP (50,000) records. The agent's byte arithmetic puts HashMap<Box<str>, u32> x 50k at roughly 2.5-3.5MB, i.e. probably over budget. The #[ignore]d soak test exists but has not been run. Needs a main-agent run of `cargo nextest run -p ime-dict --run-ignored all`, then one of: a more compact key representation, a lower HYDRATE_CAP, or a corrected budget number (a budget change is a main-agent call, not a sub-agent one).
cross_task_notes.data/user-db/large and data/commit/slow-: PERF-P0.02.01 defined LARGE_STORE_CODE = "data/user-db/large" and reports that data/commit/slow-disk is likewise unregistered. Both are stable codes that diagnostics match on, so 2.2.4 should list them. cross_task_notes.xtask/src/testd was never compiled: main.rs declared no `mod testd;` at all, so roughly 2000 lines across testd/{mod,input,keys,x11,coords,engine,sandbox} had never been type-checked. The main agent mounted it (`mod testd;` + a `Testd` subcommand). cross_task_notes.check-ui-spec's deferral list must shrin: UI-OPT-P0.01.01 landed scripts/check-ui-spec.sh, which asserts the 3.1.1 size table, the 3.2 colour table three ways (spec <-> theme.slint evaluated with Slint's own rounding <-> theme.rs), the 3.1.4 4dp grid plus its 12-item exception list, and a reference-closure check. The gate fails on any NEW dead name, so the list may only shrink; the cards that wire those hosts (P1.05.01, P2.03.01) must delete their entries.
cross_task_notes.cargo deny check is not wired into any C: deny.toml exists and `cargo deny check` reports advisories ok / bans ok / licenses ok / sources ok, but nothing invokes it: check-advisories is deliberately NOT in `just ci` (cargo audit needs the network), and the CI `quality` job installs cargo-deny yet never calls it. The right home is the `audit` job, the only networked one -- it already installs the tools. Main-agent work; ci.yml was owned by a running agent when this was found.
cross_task_notes.check-no-network.sh lacks the getrandom: RESOLVED QUESTION (main agent ran the measurement): the card asks for a getrandom-by-feature rule (rejecting the js / wasm_js entropy sources). `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --all-features` shows getrandom present twice -- 0.3.4 and 0.4.3 -- and BOTH resolve with features = ['std'] only; neither has wasm_js on. So the rule can be written against the resolved feature list without false-positiving on this graph. The earlier hesitation (that --all-features without --filter-platform makes a node's feature list a cross-platform union) is real in general but does not bite here, because wasm_js is an opt-in feature that nothing in the workspace turns on. Still to do: add the rule and a self-test case to scripts/check-no-network.sh, which is now free.
cross_task_notes.Effect::AddPhrase has two unconsumed mat: ADD-FEAT-P0.01.03 added `Effect::AddPhrase { key, text }` to the session's effect enum, whose doc comment says the pair 'leaves as an effect and the host layer appends it to the user's phrase document'. Two exhaustive matches now fail to compile: `crates/ime-fcitx5/src/engine/router.rs`'s `apply_effects` (the host layer, and the file that must do the appending) and `crates/ime-core/src/state/tests.rs`'s `kind()` helper (the test-side name table). Both are outside that card's whitelist and are the main agent's to close. They are deliberately NOT closed yet: the phrase module is read-only so far (`PhraseTable::parse`/`load`/`longest_match`, no writer), so an arm written now would either be a silent no-op or would have to invent the writer's interface before its owner has defined it. Wire both once ADD-FEAT-P0.01.03 reports.
cross_task_notes.Slint's software renderer ignores `opaci: Measured, not inferred. In crates/ime-ui/ui/candidate_grid.slint, setting a Text element's `opacity` to 0.1 -- and then replacing the opacity with a colour built by with-alpha(0.1) -- leaves the sampled ink of the rendered cell at 515,630 against 515,833 for its enabled twin, a 0.04% difference. Neither form dims anything. Consequences that are live today: 3.1.1's number label at 0.55 and 3.2's text.annotation at 0.50 are drawn at full strength, and 3.4's Disabled row at 0.32 is not dimmed. check-ui-spec.sh does not catch this because it asserts the token values in the .slint SOURCE, which are correct. The grid still carries the factor (a `dim` property folded into every child that draws) because the source is where the specification is checked; TASK-1.05.05's opacity assertion was narrowed to the model-level fact it can observe, and the limitation is written into the test. A follow-up card should decide whether to render the dimming some other way (a colour alpha that the renderer honours, or a compositing step) or to record the deviation against 3.1.1/3.2/3.4.

tasks.title: 用户数据目录与文件权限基线
tasks.note: merged: paths.rs (784 lines, 18 tests) + perms.rs (283 lines, 10 tests). Layering respected -- paths.rs depends only on ime-types, perms.rs only on std, neither imports the other. Modes are set at creation (OpenOptions::mode / DirBuilder::mode), so there is no window where a file exists world-readable; an existing loose file is narrowed through its own fd. Symlinks below the XDG base are refused and neither the link nor its target is touched; the base directories themselves are the trust root and are never chmod'd, because putting $HOME on another volume is a legitimate layout. Two diagnostic codes are defined in both files because the layer order forbids sharing them -- a single source would mean promoting them into the frozen ime-types, which needs an ADR. PENDING: criterion 3 needs StatusStrip.readonly wired at the addon, and criterion 5's 5ms probe needs a gate run.
